subtopicTitle: Rotating frames — centrifugal force, Coriolis force

cards.front: What is the centrifugal force experienced in a frame rotating at angular velocity ω?
cards.back: Fictitious outward force F_cent = −m ω × (ω × r) = m ω² ρ (where ρ is perpendicular distance from axis). It arises because the rotating observer sees objects at rest in inertial space as accelerating inward.

cards.front: What is the Coriolis force on a mass m moving at velocity v_rel in a frame rotating at ω?
cards.back: F_Cor = −2m ω × v_rel. It is perpendicular to both ω and v_rel, deflects moving objects to the right in the Northern Hemisphere (ω has upward component).

cards.front: Write the full effective force equation in a rotating frame (including Euler term).
cards.back: F_eff = F_real − m ω × (ω × r) − 2m ω × v_rel − m (dω/dt) × r. The last term is the Euler force when ω changes.

cards.front: Derive the centrifugal acceleration term from the second time derivative of position in rotating vs inertial frames.
cards.back: r_inertial = R(t) r_rot. Differentiate twice: a_in = a_rot + 2ω×v_rot + ω×(ω×r) + (dω/dt)×r. Thus a_rot = a_in − ω×(ω×r) − 2ω×v − … so fictitious acceleration includes +ω²ρ outward.

cards.front: In the Northern Hemisphere, which way does the Coriolis force deflect a projectile moving eastward?
cards.back: To the right (southward component). Eastward velocity crossed with upward ω produces a southward fictitious force.

cards.front: Why does the effective g decrease at the equator due to rotation?
cards.back: Centrifugal acceleration mω²R outward opposes gravity. At equator ρ = R, so g_eff ≈ g − ω²R (≈ 0.034 m/s² reduction).

cards.front: For an object at rest in the rotating frame, which fictitious force remains and why does the Coriolis term vanish?
cards.back: Only centrifugal force acts. v_rel = 0 so −2mω×v_rel = 0. Coriolis requires relative motion.

cards.front: State the condition under which the Euler force appears and give its vector expression.
cards.back: When angular velocity changes: F_Euler = −m (dω/dt) × r. Present during spin-up or precession of the frame.
